chunks: And it is narrated from Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
“Supplicate with this supplication for the absconding slave, and write it on a sheet of paper:

O Allah, the heaven is Yours, and the earth is Yours, and whatever is between them is Yours; so make what is between them tighter upon so-and-so than the skin of a camel, until You return him to me and grant me mastery over him.
And let Āyat al-Kursī be written around the writing in a circular manner, then bury it and place something heavy over it in the place where he used to take shelter at night.”

key_terms.آيَةُ الْكُرْسِيِّ: Āyat al-Kursī, to be written around the text
key_terms.السَّمَاءُ: the heaven, invoked as belonging to Allah
key_terms.الْأَرْضُ: the earth, affirmed as belonging to Allah
key_terms.بِاللَّيْلِ: at night, describing the place of shelter
key_terms.وَرَقَةٍ: a sheet of paper on which the supplication is written

ai.seo_question: What supplication is narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام for an absconding slave?
ai.summary: This hadith transmits a specific du'a to be recited and written for an absconding slave, invoking Allah’s dominion over the heavens, the earth, and all that lies between them. It also instructs writing Āyat al-Kursī around the text and burying it in a particular place, presenting a devotional practice tied to recovery of the runaway.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3545 - Mu'awiyah ibn Ammar narrated from Abu Abdullah (as):
"Recite this supplication for the runaway slave and write it down on a piece of paper:

'O Allah (swt)! The heavens belong to You, the earth belongs to You, and whatever is between them belongs to You. Make what is between them tighter upon [slave's name] than the skin of a camel, until You return him to me and make me victorious over him.'
Then, write Ayat al-Kursi around the paper in a circular manner. Bury it and place something heavy over it in the spot where he used to take shelter at night."
